messages.subject: mtpc analyses plots not showing null permutations at one specific threshold
messages.subject_clean: mtpc analyses plots not showing null permutations at one specific threshold
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have run a mtpc analysis (testing for weighted global efficiency difference) with 5000 permutations across 6 thresholds and have noticed that one threshold almost only gets 1 to 2 maximum null statistics.

I tried running 3000000 permutations which does increase the amount at thresh .26 but in a markedly smaller range compared to the other thresholds. Is that an expected behaviour or is there something wrong happening with the plotter?

I tried looking at the matrices thresholded at .26 and there is nothing wrong with them.
I tried looking at the null.dist, its summary statistics, and if I'm not mistaken I should expect a contrast in the second to last 5000 permutations (as .26 is second to last threshold), but nothing unusual appears:

Similarly, looking into the stats ($DT) of the mtpc object does not suggest anything changes at that specific threshold. I also tried looking at the E.glob.wt values per subject across each threshold, and global efficiency barely changes .22,.26.30 thresholds. Everything lets me think there's nothing special about that threshold.

Is it simply a product of the randomness of graph data? Or could the R plotter have difficulties with it?

Best regards,
Charly

messages.subject: Clarifying Contrast and Alternative calls on NBS()
messages.subject_clean: Clarifying Contrast and Alternative calls on NBS()
messages.body_plain:
Chris,

I could use some help understanding the T.mat and p.mat structures in terms of "alternative" hypothesis and contrasts.

I am looking to compare two cohorts and adjust for age and sex. My contrast matrix is

con.mat <- cbind(0, 0, 0, c(-1, 1))
rownames(con.mat) <- c('HC > PA', 'PA  > HC')

I want to find
what edges are different between PA and HC
what edges are stronger in PA than HC
what edges are weaker in PA than HC
So my questions are:
Would it be best to alter the contrast which sets direction of comparison or alter the "alternative" call?
Can I call "greater" or "less" with the same contrast matrix?
this works for "greater" but "less" causes an error
Error in factor(contrast, labels = tmp$con.name <http://con.name>) : invalid 'labels'; length 2 should be 1 or 0
The "two.sided" T.mat structure is NxNx2  and is just a sign difference (T.mat[,,1]=-T.mat[,,2]). This suggests it would be easy to threshold at T[,,1]>=2 or T[,,2]<=-2 and for edge indices that are "different" between the two groups, correct?
In "greater", T.mat[,,1] is not equal to =T.mat[,,2].
For "Greater", is T.mat[,,1] giving the t-test statistics for edges where PA>HC, and T.mat[,,2] giving the t-test statistics for edges where HC>PA?
Would this be flipped for "less" (if it was not producing an error?)
Thank you for any help,

messages.body_plain:
Following up on this.

I have read the links on contrast coding attempting to apply it to NBS() to find edges that are (1) different (2) stronger in impaired or (3) stronger in unimpaired. I have shifted from using "effects" to "dummy" for simplicity. Also, if I use "dummy" I sometimes get the error " Error in factor(contrast, labels = tmp$con.name <http://con.name>) : invalid 'labels'; length 2 should be 1 or 0 " for some comparisons depending on "alternative" choice. I  think this is happening when one dimension of the contrast does not have significant results. I am unsure but based on using the dummy coding, it seems to align.

My covar table looks like
data_i_table
Study.ID    Age      Sex    Impairment
<num>    <num>  <fctr>       <fctr>

Relevant Code
con.mat<-cbind(0,0,0,1)
rownames(con.mat) <- c('Impaired vs Unimpaired')
X_spec <- brainGraph_GLM_design(data_i_table, coding='dummy',binarize=c('Sex'))
res.nbs.two <- NBS(A=cm_Use, covars=data_i_table, contrasts=con.mat,con.type="t", X=X_spec,p.init=0.001, N=5000, alternative="two.sided")

For the most part, I think this is working but there are some checks that didnt make sense.
e.g. For a "two.sided" comparison here, shouldn't contrast of [0 0 0 1] and [0 0 0 -1] be the same? If not, what is the difference here, because NBS() returns different results? It should basically mean either u1-u2!=0 or u2-u1!=0
e.g. Shouldnt a [0 0 0 1] of a "greater" comparison be the same as a [ 0 0 0 -1] of a "less" comparison?  Similarly, u1-u2>0 should convert to u2-u1<0?

Thank you,
